summary.intent: Continue improving callisto: first finish stacking open PRs correctly (#360, #361, #363, with #359 independent), then pursue amazing performance, great DX and reliability by measuring and optimizing the CLI against real workloads.
summary.outcome: Built a native GitHub stack #360 → #361 → #363 (merged without force-push, `just ci` green), then opened a new performance PR that loads the workspace once, runs the ls-remote tag probe on a scoped thread, and parallelizes release observation loops and the moved-past-version check; CI passed locally.

repo: Open PRs #361 and #363 both edit `init.rs`, its tests, `docs/errors.md` and `error.rs`, so they must be stacked rather than left independent; #359 touches different files and stays on `main`.
A pre-commit hook rejects broken files, so a bad merge resolution did not commit and nothing broken was pushed.
`just ci` is the full local check (includes clippy, which flags collapsible `if`s); a `bench` recipe exists for command benchmarks.
`CommandRunner` is already `Send + Sync`, and the provider context types are `Sync`, so observation loops can be parallelized without extra bounds.
`cargo info` costs ~100 ms per call and barely parallelizes because cargo takes a lock; PyPI observation already uses direct HTTP, so the Cargo path is a candidate for the same approach.
In a single-package `release --dry-run` with no tags the ls-remote probe did not run, so another part of the plan (the tag provider's ls-remote observation) also makes the network call.
#360 also edits `release/local.rs`, so overlap with the perf PR had to be checked before shipping.

code.finding: Added `plan_loaded_release` entry point that reuses an already-loaded workspace and keeps the registry name check; exported through `commands/mod.rs`.
Added an order-preserving bounded worker helper (`in_parallel`) used by three observation loops; also exposed for the per-package moved-past-version check.
CLI release entry now loads the workspace once, starts the tag-missing-from-origin probe on a scoped thread, then plans with the loaded workspace.
Merge of #361 into #363 conflicted because both sides add tests at the same spot; scripted resolution dropped a closing brace and a `#[test]` line.

workflow: When stacking PRs with overlapping edits, merge each branch into the one above it and push without force-push.
A scripted conflict resolution can produce invalid code; run the relevant tests immediately after resolving, before committing.
Measure before optimizing: benchmark, list process shapes per command and profile external processes with shims, then re-time after each change.
Check overlap with open PR branches before opening a new PR touching shared files.
Reproduce reported issues before building; unreproducible items (E121 message) were dropped.

friction: Scripted merge conflict resolution produced invalid Rust and was nearly committed; the hook caught it.
The first perf probe had no effect in the single-package case because a different code path made the network call, requiring a hunt for all ls-remote call sites.
`cargo info` serializes on a cargo lock, limiting the parallelism gain for the Cargo path.
Clippy flagged a collapsible `if` that required an extra CI round.
open_items: Python `~=` precision and Poetry comment loss: to be reproduced before building, skipped if not reproducible.
Cargo registry observation could use a direct HTTP call (as PyPI does) instead of `cargo info` to avoid the lock bottleneck.
Merge #360, #361, #363 in order and retarget as GitHub prompts; #359 and the new perf PR are awaiting review/merge.
Continue the performance and DX dogfooding on real repositories.
